assumptions: Field labels (+0x198 buffer, record array, string vectors) describe observed pointer arithmetic only, not confirmed source-level types.
Sized-delete sizes are the second argument observed at each PLT call site.
behavior: object member teardown: destroys the object's members in a fixed order, never frees the object itself, never reads a vtable slot, performs no canary check

consumers.note: Reached only by code, never by data. See callers.tsv for the site list.

observations: No direct or PLT call other than 0x5f3c850, 0x5d8d820, 0x5d35c30, 0x5d350c0 and the sized-delete PLT 0x63f0d80.
No indirect dispatch: no vtable slot is read anywhere in the routine.

Distinct from the neighbouring 0x5d573f0 member-tree teardown (covered by #2719): that routine unrolls a 9-level tree walk with self-recursion over 0x58-byte nodes; this routine walks a flat record array plus four independent member vectors and has no recursion.

reset-capable buffer: end +0x1a0 set to begin when different, then free (begin, +0x1a8 - begin) when begin non-null
loop over records with stride 0x218 (see record_fields)
free (begin, +0x140 - begin) when begin non-null; no end reset
zeroed when nonzero (flag clear, not a free)
reset-capable buffer: end +0x120 set to begin when different, then free (begin, +0x128 - begin) when begin non-null
free (begin, +0xa8 - begin) when begin non-null; no end reset
free (begin, +0x90 - begin) when begin non-null; no end reset

free (begin, +0x60 - begin) when begin non-null; no end reset

stride 0x40; per element call 0x5d350c0 with the +0x38 pointer when non-null (call-shape only), then dispose the +0x08 string (short-form address element +0x18); then free the buffer (begin, +0x48 - begin) when begin non-null

stride 0x40; per element dispose the +0x20 string (short-form address element +0x30) then the +0x00 string (short-form address element +0x10); then the buffer exit (free via tail jump, or plain return when null)

per_record.action: when non-null, call 0x5d8d820 with the pointer (call-shape only), then sized delete 0x290

reverse walk: index count-1 down to 0, stride 0x30, dispose each string (short-form address element +0x10); count stored back each step, ending at 0; the array buffer itself is NOT freed by this routine
forward dispose pass, stride 0x30, same string rule; end +0x200 reset to begin when the vector is non-empty; buffer freed (begin, +0x208 - begin) when begin non-null
a second loop over the same +0x1f8 range is present but unreachable: its entry test compares the reloaded begin against the same begin value, so it always jumps to the buffer free
zeroed when nonzero (flag clear, not a free)
reset-capable buffer: end +0x58 set to begin when different, then free (begin, +0x60 - begin) when begin non-null; the record pointer is advanced to the next record before this free

string_rule.heap_form: sized delete (pointer, capacity + 1), capacity at string + 0x10
string_rule.short_form: data pointer equals string address + 0x10; frees nothing

unknowns: The semantic roles of the 0x5f3c850, 0x5d8d820, 0x5d35c30 and 0x5d350c0 callees are not pinned; they are recorded as call-shape only.
The +0x1f0 string array's buffer ownership is not pinned: its strings are disposed here but its buffer is not freed here.
